title: Trained fly visual-system connectome models keep their motion tuning with the column-offset synapse profiles of two other flies, but lose it when type-pair synapse totals change (10 flyvis models)
abstract: Question: the 50 pretrained flyvis models of the fly visual system (Lappalainen et al. 2024) take fixed synapse counts per cell-type pair and column offset from one 7-column FIB-25/FIB-19 reconstruction. Do their predictions stay the same with the counts of other optic lobes? Approach: we computed the same per-offset count table for FlyWire v783 (both eyes, 31 column-assigned types) and male CNS v1.0 (both eyes, 28 types; columns of 16 types from a partner rule calibrated on FlyWire), aligned the hex lattices, and replaced the 710 model keys between these types (46% of model synapse mass) in the 10 best models. We split each change into the offset profile inside a type pair (shape) and the type-pair totals (gain), and used a within-pair offset permutation as a positive control and random nulls. Read-outs were flash polarity and moving-edge direction tuning, compared with the flyvis ground-truth lists from experiments (270 simulations). Results: the four large optic lobes agreed with each other (log-SD per key 0.22-0.34, similar to left vs right) and all differed from FIB25 (0.53-0.56), within the noise of a 7-column sample (0.75). All real tables and their consensus lowered the agreement of DSI with known motion tuning (r 0.68 to 0.19-0.50; p 0.004-0.049) and the T4/T5 subtypes with the correct preferred direction (median 5.5 to 2.5-4.5 of 8), and silenced some T4/T5 cells, but did not change flash polarity agreement. Gain-only tables reproduced all of this damage. Shape-only tables changed nothing (response change 0.001), although random offset permutation lowered DSI agreement in 10 of 10 models. The pre-specified test that real differences are less disruptive than random ones failed (1 of 4 tests). Limitation: no retraining (2 CPUs); because trained type-pair strengths multiply the totals, retrained models may absorb the gain differences. One speed, dt 0.01 s, 10 of 50 models.

display.caption: Ten flyvis models with synapse counts from FlyWire and male CNS optic lobes. A-C: agreement with known flash polarity and T4/T5 direction tuning, and silent T4/T5 subtypes, for the original FIB25 counts and six real tables. D-E: shape-only tables (new offset profile, FIB25 type-pair totals) change nothing; gain-only tables reproduce the full damage; within-pair offset permutation is a positive control. F: real vs random-null response change. G-H: post hoc restoration of FIB25 inputs to T4/T5. Grey dots are models; red bars are medians.

A: SD of log count difference per key between the FIB25 table of the models and four large optic lobes (FlyWire R* uses partner-assigned columns). B: a 7-column FlyWire sample differs from its full optic lobe more than FIB25 does. C: type-pair input totals onto T4 and T5 relative to FIB25.

Model 000: peak responses of T4a-d (ON edges) and T5a-d (OFF edges) to edges moving in 12 directions with FIB25, FlyWire R, male CNS R and consensus counts, and with the FlyWire R shape-only and gain-only tables.
